title: privacy: review the Datenschutzerklärung against actual retention
description:
Open-source contribution opportunity. Repository: Open-LEG-ch/openleg. Labels: documentation, help wanted, privacy, ready-for-human. ## Why

The retention matrix in #530 documents what deletion code and schema constraints actually reach. Open issues #550 and #551 identify two claims that overstate deletion behavior. A legal or data-protection owner must review the full Datenschutzerklärung and choose wording or policy; code inspection cannot make that judgment.

Blocked by: none.

## Human work

- Review every retention and deletion claim against `docs/retention-matrix.md`.
- Resolve the wording decisions in #550 and #551 as part of the review.
- Confirm legal bases, retention periods, controller and processor wording, and hosting-level log claims with the responsible owners.
- File separate implementation issues for approved copy or behavior changes.

## Done when

- A named legal or DPO reviewer records approval and the review date.
- Each matrix row has matching public wording or a documented reason why no wording is needed.
- #550 and #551 have approved resolutions.
- Follow-up issues quote the exact current location and approved replacement, without customer data.

title: test: add tests for gdpr_compliance.rego (GDPR)
description:
Open-source contribution opportunity. Repository: ynotbhatc/rego_policy_libraries. Labels: help wanted, good first issue. **File:** `frameworks/privacy/gdpr/gdpr_compliance.rego` (292 lines)
**Package:** `gdpr.compliance`
**Standard:** GDPR

This policy uses **boolean rules**: `default <name> := false` with a matching
`<name> if { ... }`. There are roughly **21** of them.

For each, write a case with input that makes it true, and one where it stays
false. Boolean rules are where the `{}` trap bites — a rule with no `default`
is *undefined* rather than false, and one undefined field collapses the whole
report object.

### Done when

- [ ] `opa test frameworks/privacy/gdpr -v` passes
- [ ] Each rule has a case that exercises it
- [ ] At least one case asserts nothing fires on compliant input
- [ ] The compliance report is asserted to be a **populated object on empty input**, not `{}`

### Where to put it

`frameworks/privacy/gdpr/tests/test_gdpr_compliance.rego`, package `gdpr.compliance_test`.

The pattern to copy, and the `array.concat` trap, are in
[CONTRIBUTING.md](../blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md). The full queue of untested
policies is in [COVERAGE.md](../blob/main/COVERAGE.md).

---

*Comment before you start so two people don't write the same test.*

title: corpus(tier1): expand court-documented legal AI citation failures
description:
Open-source contribution opportunity. Repository: yenklabs/Dali. Labels: help wanted, benchmark, research. ## Problem
Tier 1 currently contains a small set of canonical legal AI citation failures.
The benchmark should expand carefully using only:
- court-documented incidents
- canonically retrievable authorities
- reproducible source URLs
- stable citation metadata

---

## Requirements for scoring-eligible additions
Each record should include:
- authoritative source URL
- retrieval timestamp
- canonical citation metadata
- reproducible verification path
- documented judicial or regulatory context

---

## Non-goals
Do NOT add:
- social-media anecdotes
- unverifiable claims
- media summaries without underlying authority
- speculative incidents

---

## Potential future additions
- sanctions orders
- judicial findings involving fabricated citations
- disciplinary proceedings
- verified filing incidents involving non-existent authorities

title: Add industry file: Legal Tech
description:
Open-source contribution opportunity. Repository: glacierphonk/naming. Labels: enhancement, help wanted, good first issue, industry. ## Task

Add a legal tech naming guide at \`industries/legaltech.md\`. Depends on #180.

## Why legal tech naming is distinct

- **Authority and gravitas required** — lawyers are conservative buyers. Playful names feel unserious
- **Latin legal vocabulary** — massive untapped naming source (habeas, certiorari, amicus, pro bono — but also pretentious if misused)
- **Trust + precision** — legal products handle sensitive documents, contracts, privileged communications
- **Regulated profession** — \"attorney\" and \"lawyer\" have legal meaning. Names that imply legal advice when the product doesn't provide it are risky
- **Old industry meets new tech** — naming must bridge tradition and innovation

## Sections to cover

- Case studies: Harvey (AI), Clio, Ironclad, Everlaw, LegalZoom, Rocket Lawyer
- Anti-patterns: \"Legal[X]\", \"[X]Law\", fake Latin, over-gravitas
- Territory map: Shield/protection, compass/guidance, ledger/record, bridge/arbitration

## Before submitting

Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) and run \`markdownlint-cli2 '**/*.md'\` before pushing.
